A second source agrees, none contradicts
open_items: College sport-level weights were re-measured with topic terms after the first review; the small regional sports (hockey, wrestling, volleyball, lacrosse) still sit at the detection floor relative to the NFL anchor, so their sport-level weights are upper bounds

Families with fewer than half of their team-by-state cells detected (the rest censored, carried as bounded floors): bsb, cbb_m, cbb_w, cfb, hky_m, hky_w, lax, pwhl, sfb, vbw, wrs, so shares for these rest on few detected cells

Dominance of the lead pair biggest matchup, as measured: IL->WI: inconclusive (corrected measure lacks comparable units); WI->IL: inconclusive (too few detected units or low detected coverage) (a direction is inconclusive without at least three detected units covering 80% of the model mass and, for the corrected measure, comparable units)

Second proxies for that dominance: IL->WI | Google comparison searches ('A vs B') DISAGREES; IL->WI (national readership) | Wikipedia rivalry-article readership, 2021 to 2025 agrees; WI->IL | Google comparison searches ('A vs B') DISAGREES; WI->IL (national readership) | Wikipedia rivalry-article readership, 2021 to 2025 agrees. A same-platform proxy that contradicts blocks the gate; the independent Wikipedia proxy is national and carries no geography
The refined single-matchup rule: its text was written before the channel measurements but it was adopted after seeing them and after the original edge-removal gate had failed for the lead pair

The model over-concentrates hostility on one marquee matchup in most testable directions (see docs/CHANNEL_DECOMPOSITION.md), and the leading pair changes under the flat-tier prior and under flat sport weights

The Monte Carlo samples measurement and parameter noise but not structural alternatives (tier ladder, sport weights), so the probability of finishing first is conditional on the model structure; the relevant-leave-out gate is threshold-dependent (driver share at least 5%; at 2.5% the result would be: 3 of 4 keep it in the top 5)

Monte Carlo noise for edges is derived from the model misfit on NFL, MLB and NBA teams (in-sample) and applied to every edge; per-sport systematic multipliers (sd 0.30) are my own choice and not identifiable from team-level data

The identity layer E (which state a team stands for) has only an exploratory measurement (embodiment index for 40 teams and schools; the Bears are +0.46 against +0.80 for the Packers while E gives both 0.95 to their home state)

The corroboration thresholds were fixed before their table was computed but after the lead pairs state-level ranks were already known; the state-level rank is out of the 677 pairs measured in both directions; the searches-only check was inconclusive for most of the top pairs; the place factor was fixed after a first look at the estimates and replicated only on college schools
Raw Google Trends payloads are not published, so a stranger cannot rebuild the results from the repository alone; only stages downstream of the cache are reproducible
Three independent reviews were completed (2026-10-16, 2026-10-17, 2026-10-18) and their findings addressed (see CHANGELOG)
